questions.question: Mehrunnisa married Emperor Jahangir in
questions.solution:
• In 1611, Jahangir married Mehrunnisa, who was known as Nur Jahan (Light of the World).
  • She encouraged Persian art and culture in the court.

questions.question: The Battle of Samugarh was fought between Aurangzeb and which Mughal prince?
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Samugarh (29 May 1658) was fought between Aurangzeb and Dara Shikoh.
  • It was part of the Mughal war of succession after Shah Jahan fell ill.
  • Dara Shikoh was defeated, paving the way for Aurangzeb's capture of Agra and later imprisonment of Shah Jahan.

questions.question: Identify the Mughal emperor who was imprisoned for the rest of his life in Agra after the war of succession among his sons.
questions.solution:
• Shah Jahan was imprisoned for the rest of his life in Agra Fort after the war of succession.
  • Aurangzeb declared himself emperor in 1658 and imprisoned Shah Jahan until his death in January 1666.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the succession of Shah Jahan:
Statement 1: Shah Jahan chose his eldest son Dara Shikoh as his successor to the Mughal throne.
Statement 2: Dara Shikoh defeated Aurangzeb in the Battle of Deorai (1659) and became emperor.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Shah Jahan nominated his eldest son Dara Shikoh as his successor.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Aurangzeb defeated Dara Shikoh in the Battle of Deorai (1659). Dara was executed, and Aurangzeb ascended the throne.

questions.question: Who among the following has written the 'Badshah Nama'?
questions.solution:
• Abdul Hamid Lahori wrote the 'Badshah Nama' (Padshahnama).
  • He was a historian and traveler who became a court historian of Shah Jahan.
  • The Padshahnama is the official history of Shah Jahan's reign.

questions.question: The mausoleum of the Taj Mahal was designed by
questions.solution:
• Ustad Ahmad Lahori was the chief Mughal architect during Shah Jahan's reign.
  • He was responsible for the construction of the Taj Mahal in Agra and the Red Fort in Delhi.

questions.question: The art of decoration called Pietra dura became popular during whose reign?
questions.solution:
• Pietra dura became popular during Shah Jahan's reign.
  • Pietra dura is an inlay technique using cut and fitted, highly polished colored stones to create images.
  • Other buildings by Shah Jahan: Red Fort (Delhi), Jama Masjid (Delhi), Shish Mahal (Agra), Shalimar Bagh (Lahore).

questions.question: Ahmadnagar was finally annexed by the Mughals in
questions.solution:
• Ahmadnagar was finally annexed by the Mughals in 1632 during Shah Jahan's period.
  • Malik Ahmed was the founder of Ahmadnagar (Maharashtra), who established the Nizam Shahi dynasty.

questions.question: Who among the following had been given the title of 'Sultan Buland Iqbal' by Shah Jahan?
questions.solution:
• Dara Shikoh (eldest son of Shah Jahan) was given the title 'Sultan Buland Iqbal' (Prince of High Fortune) on 10 September 1642.
  • His works include Majma-ul-Bahrain (Mingling of Two Oceans) and Sirr-i-Akbar (Great Mystery).
  • He was executed in 1659 by Aurangzeb in the war of succession.

questions.question: Which Mughal Emperor issued the Deccan campaign against the Marathas and spent significant time in the region?
questions.solution:
• Aurangzeb (1658-1707) launched the most extensive Deccan campaign in Mughal history.
  • After Shivaji's death in 1680, Aurangzeb personally moved to the Deccan and remained there for 27 years (1680-1707) until his death at Ahmednagar.
  • He annexed Bijapur (1686) and Golconda (1687).
  • The prolonged war drained the Mughal treasury and is considered a major reason for the decline of the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Which Mughal ruler was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in the year 1675?
questions.solution:
• Aurangzeb was responsible for the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur in 1675.
  • Guru Tegh Bahadur was the ninth Sikh Guru, often venerated as the 'Protector of Humanity' (Srisht-di-Chadar) by the Sikhs.
  • He founded Anandpur Sahib.

questions.question: Under whose rule did the Mughal empire achieve its largest territorial limits?
questions.solution:
• The Mughal Empire achieved its largest territorial limits under Aurangzeb (1658-1707).
  • He ascended the throne in 1658 after eliminating all competitors including Dara Shukoh, Shuja, and Murad.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rathor Rajputs of Marwar:
Statement 1: The rebellion of the Rathor Rajputs of Marwar began due to Akbar's interference in their succession politics.
Statement 2: Babur suppressed the Rathor rebellion of Marwar during his reign.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Both statements are false.
  • The Rathor Rajput rebellion of Marwar occurred due to Aurangzeb's interference in their internal politics and succession disputes.
  • Akbar maintained friendly alliances with Rajputs; Babur fought mainly against Afghan and Rajput confederacies.

questions.question: Under which of the following Mughal emperors were the Marathas a major challenge to the sovereignty of the Mughals?
questions.solution:
• Under Aurangzeb (Reign: 1658-1707), the Marathas became a major challenge to Mughal sovereignty.
  • Aurangzeb was also known as Zinda Pir (living saint), Fakir, and Darbesh.
  • He gave the French permission to build a factory in Surat in 1667.

questions.question: Under whose reign was the maximum number of books in Persian on classical Indian Music written?
questions.solution:
• The maximum number of books in Persian on classical Indian Music were written under Aurangzeb's reign (1658-1707).
  • He reimposed Jizya and Pilgrim tax in 1679 and ended the celebration of Navroz.

questions.question: Which Mughal Emperor has attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora?
questions.solution:
• Aurangzeb (Alamgir, original name Muhi al-Din Muhammad, 1658-1707) attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora.
  • He stopped music and alcohol in the court and also the activities of 'darshan' (public audience).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Guru Nanak Dev Ji:
Statement 1: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the third Sikh Guru and Guruprab marks his birth anniversary.
Statement 2: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first Sikh Guru and the founder of Sikhism.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first Sikh Guru, not the third.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first Sikh Guru and the founder of Sikhism.
  • He was born in 1469 at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib, Pakistan). Guruprab celebrates his birth anniversary.

questions.question: After the death of Shri Guru Gobind Singh, the Sikhs revolted against the ______ under the leadership of Banda Bahadur.
questions.solution:
• After Guru Gobind Singh's death, the Sikhs revolted against the Mughals under the leadership of Banda Bahadur.
  • Guru Gobind Singh is famous for creating the Khalsa (Pure), the military brotherhood of the Sikhs.

questions.question: Who among the following Sikh spiritual gurus is said to have assisted Khusrau, the rebellious son of Jahangir?
questions.solution:
• Guru Arjun Dev assisted Khusrau, the rebellious son of Jahangir.
  • He compiled the first official edition of the Sikh scripture called the Adi Granth, which later expanded into the Guru Granth Sahib.
  • He completed the construction of the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

questions.question: Who among the following Sikh Gurus laid the foundation of 'Khalsa Panth'?
questions.solution:
• Guru Gobind Singh laid the foundation of 'Khalsa Panth' on April 13, 1699, in Punjab.
  • Khalsa Panth is the name given to the religious structure and community that manages the affairs of the global Khalsa community.

questions.question: Which Maratha ruler founded the Maratha Empire in 1674, proclaiming himself Chhatrapati?
questions.solution:
• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj founded the Maratha Empire in 1674.
  • Through guerrilla tactics and strategic battles, he established an independent Swarajya.
  • At Raigad Fort, he was coronated and assumed the title Chhatrapati.
  • Sambhaji was Shivaji's eldest son; Shahu was Shivaji's grandson; Bajirao I was a famous Peshwa.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Maratha revenue system:
Statement 1: Bhoga was the twenty-five percent land revenue collected by the Marathas in the Deccan.
Statement 2: Sardeshmukhi was an additional ten percent levy on lands where the Marathas claimed hereditary rights.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Chauth (not Bhoga) was the twenty-five percent tax imposed by the Marathas.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Sardeshmukhi was an additional 10% levy on lands under Maratha hereditary claims.
  • Bhoga belonged to the Gupta period and was a tax on gifts, fruits, flowers, etc.

questions.question: Baji Rao I or Baji Rao Ballal was the son of
questions.solution:
• Baji Rao I was the son of Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath (1713-1720).
  • Balaji Vishwanath was the first of a line of hereditary Peshwas from the Bhat family.
  • Baji Rao I (1720-1740) was the seventh Peshwa and one of the greatest exponents of guerrilla tactics after Shivaji.

questions.question: Who among the following was a famous ruler of the Maratha dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was a famous ruler of the Maratha dynasty.
  • The Maratha Empire existed from 1674 (coronation of Shivaji) to 1818 (defeat of Peshwa Bajirao II by the British East India Company).
  • Wars fought by Shivaji: Battle of Pratapgad (1659), Battle of Purandar (1665), Battle of Sinhagad (1670), Battle of Sangamner (1679).

questions.question: Which confederation of Sultanates defeated the Vijayanagara Empire in the Battle of Talikota?
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Talikota (1565) was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire (ruled by Aliya Rama Raya) and the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates - Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar, and Berar.
  • The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka Raya in 1336 AD.
